steps.title: Prepare 1.2% NaOCl solution
steps.instruction: In a laminar flow cabinet, combine 43 mL sterile Milli‑Q water, 2 mL Triton X‑100 (0.106 g/mL), and 5 mL 12 % sodium hypochlorite (12 g L⁻¹) to a final volume of 50 mL; store at 4 °C and remake every two weeks.

steps.title: Prepare 3% NaOCl solution
steps.instruction: In a laminar flow cabinet, mix 35.5 mL sterile Milli‑Q water, 2 mL Triton X‑100 (0.106 g/mL), and 15.5 mL 12 % sodium hypochlorite (37.2 g L⁻¹) to a final volume of 50 mL; store at 4 °C and remake every two weeks.

steps.title: Prepare final Hoagland solution
steps.instruction: In a sterile 1 L bottle, add 991 mL sterile Milli‑Q water, then add 2 mL of the KNO₃ stock and 1 mL of each other stock (NH₄H₂PO₄, Ca(NO₃)₂·4H₂O, MgSO₄·7H₂O, micronutrient stock, iron stock); adjust pH to 6, mix, and store at room temperature.

steps.title: Arabidopsis: Prepare germination plates
steps.instruction: In a laminar flow hood, mix 25 mL 1× Hoagland solution with 25 mL hot agar (1.3 % w/v, 6.5 g L⁻¹) to obtain 50 mL germination medium; place V3 plugs upright in each well of a sterile 24‑well plate and pipette ~5 µL medium into each plug; let cool beside the cabinet.

steps.title: Arabidopsis: Sterilize seeds
steps.instruction: Transfer a small batch of seeds to a sterile 2 mL Eppendorf tube, add 1 mL 70 % ethanol, shake 30 s, decant, then add 1 mL 1.2 % NaOCl, shake 5 min, decant, and rinse the seeds five times with autoclaved Milli‑Q water.

steps.title: Arabidopsis: Seed setup in plates
steps.instruction: Confirm the medium has solidified in the plugs, add 1 mL Hoagland solution to each well (being gentle to keep plugs upright), place sterilized seeds onto the plugs with a pipette using a small volume of sterile water (aim for two seeds per plug), seal the plate with its lid and micropore tape, wrap in aluminum foil, and place in a dark 4 °C room for 3 days (cold stratification).

steps.title: Arabidopsis: Induce shoot development
steps.instruction: Transfer plates to a growth cabinet, keep wrapped in foil for 2–3 days at 20 °C, then remove foil and grow under a photoperiod of 14 h light (26 °C) / 10 h dark (20 °C) at 110–140 µmol m⁻² s⁻¹.

steps.title: Arabidopsis: Transfer seedlings to EcoFAB
steps.instruction: After up to 5 days, when visible leaves and small roots have formed, move each seedling into an EcoFAB 2.0 reservoir using sterile forceps, taking care not to damage roots.

steps.title: Lactuca: Prepare agar plates
steps.instruction: In a laminar flow hood, mix 25 mL 1× Hoagland solution with 25 mL hot agar (1.5 % w/v, 7.5 g L⁻¹) to obtain 50 mL germination medium; dispense ~20 mL into each 90 × 25 mm sterile Petri dish, then let cool beside the cabinet.

steps.title: Lactuca: Sterilize seeds
steps.instruction: Place a small number of seeds in a sterile 2 mL tube, add 1 mL 70 % ethanol, shake 30 s, decant, add 1 mL 1.2 % NaOCl, shake 5 min, decant, and rinse five times with autoclaved Milli‑Q water.

steps.title: Lactuca: Seed setup on plates
steps.instruction: Using sterile forceps, place each sterilized seed on the agar surface with the same side facing up, seal the dish with its lid and micropore tape, wrap in aluminum foil, and cold‑stratify in a dark 4 °C room for 1 day.

steps.title: Lactuca: Induce shoots and tilt
steps.instruction: Remove foil and move plates to a growth cabinet with the same photoperiod as Arabidopsis (14 h light 26 °C / 10 h dark 20 °C, 110–140 µmol m⁻² s⁻¹); after one additional day, tilt each plate by raising the top edge 3 cm to guide roots downward, then keep in the growth chamber.

steps.title: Lactuca: Transfer seedlings to EcoFAB
steps.instruction: When radicles have emerged (≈1 week) and leaves/roots reach 1–1.5 cm, transfer seedlings into EcoFAB 2.0 reservoirs with sterile forceps, avoiding root damage.

steps.title: Fragaria: Prepare agar plates
steps.instruction: In a laminar flow hood, mix 25 mL 1× Hoagland solution with 25 mL hot agar (1.4 % w/v, 7 g L⁻¹) to obtain 50 mL germination medium; dispense ~20 mL into each 90 × 25 mm sterile Petri dish, then let cool beside the cabinet.

steps.title: Fragaria: Scarify seeds with beads
steps.instruction: Aliquot seeds into a sterile 2 mL tube, add 20 sterilized 0.5 mm borosilicate beads, and vortex for 30 s to create small abrasions on the seed coat.

steps.title: Fragaria: Sterilize seeds
steps.instruction: Transfer the scarified seeds to a sterile tube, add 1 mL 70 % ethanol, shake 30 s, decant, add 1 mL 3 % NaOCl, shake 5 min, decant, and rinse five times with autoclaved Milli‑Q water.

steps.title: Fragaria: Seed setup on plates
steps.instruction: Using sterile forceps, place each sterilized seed on the agar surface with consistent orientation, seal the dish with its lid and micropore tape, wrap in aluminum foil, and cold‑stratify in a dark 4 °C room for 1 day.

steps.title: Fragaria: Induce shoots and tilt
steps.instruction: Remove foil, move plates to a growth cabinet with the same photoperiod as above (14 h light 26 °C / 10 h dark 20 °C, 110–140 µmol m⁻² s⁻¹); after one more day, tilt each plate by raising the top edge 3 cm to direct roots downward, then keep in the growth chamber.

steps.title: Fragaria: Transfer seedlings to EcoFAB
steps.instruction: When radicle protrusion occurs (≈2 weeks) and leaves/roots reach 1–1.5 cm, move seedlings into EcoFAB 2.0 reservoirs with sterile forceps, handling roots gently.

steps.title: General: Transfer seedlings to EcoFAB
steps.instruction: For any species, when roots are about 1 cm long, gently insert the root into the EcoFAB plant reservoir using sterile forceps, avoid damage, and water carefully to prevent disturbance.

steps.title: Imaging and maintenance
steps.instruction: Capture initial whole‑plant images (e.g., smartphone), then refill the EcoFAB media every two days and maintain the defined growth conditions; acquire additional images as required for the experiment.

description: Validation of protocol For each plant, we tested different treatments to get homogeneous seedlings ready for EcoFAB setup. We applied different conditions to seeds that can improve germination. A. Arabidopsis B Arabidopsis seeds were too small to sit on the pore in EcoFab 2.0; they needed an additional surface (agar) and a plug to hold them and maintain the habitat of the plant. Initially, we used Murashige and Skoog medium but found poor results. So, we moved to Hoagland’s nutrient solution as recommended by Delden and colleagues [20]. We tried the following treatments using Hoagland’s nutrient solution to improve homogeneity and the rate of germination for Arabidopsis : 1. Seeds placed on plugs filled with growth medium and positioned on a 90 × 25 mm Petri dish. 2. Seeds placed on plugs filled with growth medium and positioned in wells of a 24-well plate filled with Hoagland’s nutrient solution. 3. Seeds placed on plugs filled with rockwool and positioned on a 90 × 25 mm Petri dish. 4. Seeds placed on plugs filled with rockwool and positioned in wells of a 24-well plate filled with Hoagland’s nutrient solution. Germination of seeds was very high for all treatments, ranging from 86.4%–93.3%. The lowest germination rates were observed on Petri dishes, where both treatments had a germination rate of 86.4%. Germination was not scored for Arabidopsis as roots were not visible on rockwool. We found no significant differences between treatments for total leaf area and our estimated leaf area per plant (leaf area/total number of plants; Figure 4 and Table S1). There were differences in the spread of data, where total leaf area (p-value = 0.03) and estimated leaf area (p-value = 0.07) of plants on 24-well plates with agar plugs were more homogeneous compared to those in other treatments ( Figure 4 and Table S2).
